key_insight: StylisticBias shows that a small set of human-style visual cues can drive most social bias judgments in multimodal LLMs. By controlling for identity and changing only appearance attributes, the paper reveals which cues most strongly influence model behavior.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of isolating appearance-based bias from identity-based differences when evaluating social bias in MLLMs. Existing benchmarks often compare different people or groups, making it hard to tell whether the model is reacting to visual style cues or to identity itself.
method: Created a controlled benchmark called StylisticBias for attribute-level social bias evaluation.
Generated 500 photorealistic base faces and systematically varied visual cues while keeping identity factors controlled.
Measured how MLLMs respond to specific human visual attributes to identify which cues most affect bias judgments.
impact: This work gives AI/ML practitioners a cleaner way to test and diagnose social bias in multimodal models. It can support safer model evaluation, more targeted mitigation strategies, and better deployment in high-stakes settings.
visual_elements: Before/after face grid showing the same identity with different visual cues
Pipeline diagram: base face -> controlled attribute edits -> MLLM judgment
Bar chart ranking which visual cues trigger the strongest bias

paper_title: StylisticBias: A Few Human Visual Cues Drive Most Social Biases in MLLMs
paper_authors: Shaghayegh Kolli, Timo Cavelius, Nafiseh Nikeghbal, Samantha Dalal, Jana Diesner
